title: Finance and Corporate Services Committee - November 24, 2025

items.title: Commencement
notes:
The Finance and Corporate Services Committee held a meeting this date commencing at 6:02 p.m.

The Chair noted the purpose of the meeting was to receive feedback from the public on the proposed 2026 Budget.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
2026 Budget - Public Consultation
notes:
I. McLean, Waterloo Region Immigration Partnership Council, addressed the Committee on behalf of the Immigration Partnership Council and highlighted the purpose and accomplishments of their organization. I. McLean noted the organization currently receives funding from the federal government, but in the most recent federal budget, there was a substantial reduction compared to previous years. As such, the organization is seeking $25,000 in funding from the City of Kitchener to help the continued implementation of the Waterloo Region Immigration Strategy and the City's future Newcomer Strategy. In response to questions from the Committee, I. McLean noted funding from the federal government was reduced to align with the level of funding provided to other immigration organizations. I. McLean further emphasized the organization's interest in a long term partnership with the City to implement newcomer and immigration initiatives. In response to questions from the Committee, D. Chapman suggested the request of the Immigration Partnership be reviewed by Council at the time Staff present the draft Newcomer Strategy. It was also noted Staff intend to recommend that the City consider partnerships with organizations carrying out immigration work. 

Councillor M. Johnston left the meeting at this time.

M. Klassen, Communitech provided comments in support of the City's continued funding for the Pitch Kitchener Initiative as proposed in the 2026 Budget. In response to questions from the Committee, M. Klassen noted Communitech is currently developing a strategy to leverage collaboration between technology companies, the public sector and the traditional economy which will allow Communitech to spread its' impact beyond the City of Kitchener. 

Councillor M. Johnston re-entered the meeting at this time.

T. LaMantia, Waterloo Economic Development Corporation provided comments in support of the City's Business Retention and Expansion program as proposed in the City's 2026 Budget. T. LaMantia suggested additional initiatives the City could consider to improve this program including hosting Kitchener specific roundtable discussions and networking events for local subsidiaries of international companies, supporting technology companies to transition into vacant office spaces within the City, and continuing to collaborate with the Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario and the Province of Ontario. In response to questions from the Committee, T. LaMantia suggested the City leverage trade diversification efforts in greenfield defense and the artificial intelligence industry. 

Councillor J. Deneault left the meeting and re-entered. 

L. Jutzi, Downtown Kitchener BIA provided comments in support of the budget proposed for the Special Events Strategy noting it will help alleviate financial pressures related to equipment rentals for special events. Further, the proposed budget will allow greater investment into cultural programming and local talent. L. Jutzi also expressed support for the budget proposed for the Business Retention and Expansion Program. 

A.M. Snider expressed concerns with the budget proposed for the Corporate Climate Action Plan (CorCap) 2.0 noting its' implementation is not a mandated responsibility of the City and further requested clarification on the funding source for the CorCap. In response to questions from the Committee, J. Readman noted, CorCap is intended to be funded through savings from completed projects such as electricity savings from converting street lights to LED lights. Additionally, the City is pursuing programs to transition existing and future facilities into net-zero, energy efficient standards which may qualify for federal and provincial grants and rebates.

items.title: Adjournment
notes:
On motion, this meeting adjourned at 7:01 p.m.

 

Marilyn Mills
Committee Coordinator
